plot: On Wheelburg's birthday Mo the mail van delivers the golden key for the old Time Box; it vanishes before noon, Bolt tests Mo, Turbo and Grumpy (all honest), then Pip insists the rule means Bolt too, and the press pops the key out from under Bolt's own hat; Bolt says sorry (lesson: admitting a mistake is brave), Pip opens the box (a kind letter and a star), then the star starts blinking.

script.title: Where Did the Golden Key Go? 🔑🕵️ Cartoon Cars for Kids
script.description: It's Wheelburg's birthday, and the golden key for the old Time Box disappears right before noon! Inspector Bolt squeezes Mo the mail van, Turbo and Grumpy in the Truth Press, until little Pip asks the bravest question of all. Saying "I made a mistake" is brave. Inspector Bolt #6

set.place: Wheelburg square, town birthday at noon

beats.say: Toot toot! Happy birthday, Wheelburg! Every car zoomed in for the big noon party!
Special delivery! One golden key, for the Wheelburg Time Box!
A Time Box? What's a Time Box?
Long ago, the town locked special things inside it. We open it on Wheelburg's birthday!
The old Time Box sat on the podium, locked tight, waiting for twelve o'clock.
I bet it's full of trophies. Probably with my face on them.
I bet it's full of dust. Old things are always dusty.
Beep beep! Inspector Bolt arrived to keep the key safe until noon.
Thank you, Mo. I will guard it myself. A detective never loses a clue.
Great! Then I'll go deliver the rest of my letters. Back in a jiffy!
Enjoy the party, everyone. The key is in very safe wheels.
Music played. Balloons popped. Everyone danced. Even Grumpy tapped one tyre.
Grumpy is dancing! Bertha, look, look!
I am not dancing. My tyre is itchy.
Then the town clock went ding, ding, ding. It was almost noon!
Inspector! It's time! Bring the golden key!
Of course. The key is right... here. Right... hmm.
Gone? But you said a detective never loses a clue!
And a detective never does. Somebody must have taken it from me.
A key thief? At a birthday party? That's so rude!
There is only one way to know. Everyone takes the Truth Press.
Mo, you brought the key. You know how special it is. You go first.
Me? I just deliver things. I never keep them! Except one stamp. A very nice stamp.
Mo, did you take the golden key?
No, Inspector. The key was for you, so I gave it to you.
Squeeze! Mo's eyes stayed small, but his letters went flying everywhere.
Oops! Now I have to deliver them all over again!
Honest. And a little messy. Next, Turbo.
Me again? I'm always a suspect. It's because I'm so good-looking.
Turbo, did you take the key?
No! I was busy dancing. Did you see my spin? Watch!
The press squeezed, and Turbo stopped spinning very fast.
Dizzy... so dizzy... but honest!
Small eyes. Thank you, Turbo. Grumpy, your turn.
I don't like keys. They're shiny. Everybody knows I hate shiny things.
Grumpy, did you take the golden key?
No. If I saw a shiny key, I'd drive the other way.
Squeeze! Grumpy's eyes stayed small and grumpy, just like always.
Three honest cars. And still no key. Most puzzling.
Tick, tock. Tick, tock. Noon was coming closer and closer.
Oh no. If we don't open the box today, we have to wait a whole year!
Wait. Inspector Bolt. You said everyone takes the Truth Press.
Yes, Pip. That is the rule. Everyone.
Then what about you? You haven't been squeezed yet!
Me? But I am the detective. I... hmm. A rule is a rule. You are right, Pip.
And for the very first time, Inspector Bolt drove into his own Truth Press.
I can't watch! Okay, I'm watching!
Inspector Bolt, did you take the golden key?
Of course not. I would never... Oh. Hmm.
His eyes! His eyes are getting bigger!
Squeeze! And out from under Bolt's hat popped... the golden key!

beats.text: THE KEY WAS IN HIS HAT!

beats.say: Oh my. I put it under my hat to keep it safe. Then I danced, and forgot.
The detective lost the clue. Under his own hat.
Everyone, I am sorry. I blamed my friends, but the mistake was mine.
That's okay, Inspector! Everybody forgets things. I forget my letters every day!
And you went into the press anyway. That was really brave.
Thank you, Pip. You followed the rule better than I did.
Saying "I made a mistake" is not small. It is one of the bravest things a car can do.
Look at the clock! It's noon! It's time!
Pip, I think you should open the Time Box today.
Me? Really? Okay! One, two, three... click!
Inside the Time Box was a letter from long ago, and a little golden star.
Read it, Pip! What does the letter say?
It says: Dear Wheelburg. Be kind, be brave, and always help each other.
That's... actually nice. Not dusty at all.
No trophies with my face. But I like it anyway!
And from now on, I keep my clues in my glove box. Not under my hat.
Everyone danced until the sun went down. But wait...
Inspector! The little star from the box just blinked at me!
Why is the star blinking? What is it trying to say? We'll find out soon!
